text:
Korean stocks dipped more than 2 percent late Monday morning, led by heavy foreign selling of technology shares amid renewed concerns over the sustainability of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom.
After opening 0.28 percent lower, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) briefly turned positive before extending its losses, falling 109.57 points, or 2.07 percent, to 5,180.96 as of 11:20 a.m.
The sell-off followed a sharp plunge in the KOSPI on Friday amid uncertainty over the future of the global AI ecosystem following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure from the company. Huang has played a pivotal role in driving the current AI boom.
Top market cap Samsung Electronics fell 2.67 percent, and chip giant SK hynix plunged 4.28 percent.
Samsung Electro-Mechanics decreased 5.96 percent, and SK Square, the parent of SK hynix, dipped 7.02 percent.
The Korean won was trading at 1,335.2 won against the U.S. dollar as of 11:20 a.m., up 2.4 won from the previous session's close.
